title: Left rotate an array by D places
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Left rotate an array by d places, in-place.
intuition: Rotation is a swap of two blocks. Reversing each block and then reversing the whole array performs that swap with no extra memory — the classic "reversal algorithm".

approaches.title: Brute: temp buffer of size d
approaches.idea: Copy the first d into a buffer, shift, append back.
approaches.code:
def rotate_left_temp(a: list[int], d: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(a)
    d %= n
    buf = a[:d]
    for i in range(d, n):
        a[i - d] = a[i]
    a[n - d:] = buf
    return a
limitations: Extra O(d) memory when d is close to n

approaches.title: Optimal: three reversals
approaches.idea: reverse(0, d-1), reverse(d, n-1), then reverse(0, n-1).
approaches.code:
def rotate_left(a: list[int], d: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(a)
    if n == 0:
        return a
    d %= n

    def reverse(lo: int, hi: int) -> None:
        while lo < hi:
            a[lo], a[hi] = a[hi], a[lo]
            lo += 1
            hi -= 1

    reverse(0, d - 1)
    reverse(d, n - 1)
    reverse(0, n - 1)
    return a
approaches.whyWorks: reverse(reverse(A) + reverse(B)) = B + A — block swap without a buffer.

specialTechnique.title: Reversal algorithm
specialTechnique.body: Any "swap two adjacent blocks in place" task (rotate array, rotate string, rotate matrix rows) reduces to three reversals. Always take d %= n first so d >= n is handled.

commonMistakes: Reversing the wrong segment boundaries for right rotation
patternRecognition: "Rotate in O(1) space" -> reversal algorithm or cyclic replacements (gcd juggling)
